Method of Attack: Info-stealing malware delivered via a fake Windows 11 upgrade ISO file
Drops multiple files including command scripts to disable security, add Defender exceptions, uninstall security products, and delete shadow volume
Establishes persistence via shortcut in Startup directory and modifies access permissions
Steals browser cookies, stored credentials, cryptocurrency wallet data, and filesystem data
Exfiltrates data encrypted via PowerShell to command and control server
Fetches additional payloads at night to steal clipboard and directory data
Impacted Systems: Windows systems capable of running Windows 11
Browsers: Chrome, Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi, 360 Browser, Comodo
Attack Vector: Poisoned search results leading to malicious website mimicking Microsoft Windows 11 upgrade page
Direct download of ISO file containing malware executable
Execution of fake Windows 11 setup executable
Indicators of Compromise: Persistence file: .LNK shortcut in Startup directory
Dropped agent file: Windows11InstallationAssistant.scr in AppData\Roaming\Windows11InstallationAssistant directory
